reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: PIB PET showed a modest -0.07 SUVr reduction in brain amyloid burden (p=0.159), suggesting some target engagement but not statistically significant. This provides weak evidence that bapineuzumab engaged amyloid beta plaques. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: CSF phospho-tau reduced by 1.38 pg/mL (p=0.620) and brain volume loss was similar between groups (p=0.884), indicating minimal downstream pathway effects despite potential target engagement. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Both primary endpoints (ADAS-Cog/11 and DAD) showed virtually no difference between treatment and placebo (p=0.979 and p=0.973 respectively), with effect sizes near zero. The trial was terminated due to lack of clinical benefit in two large Phase 3 studies. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses showed differential responses, with similar time to deterioration between groups across all timepoints. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial was adequately powered (N=1100) and duration (78 weeks) was appropriate for Alzheimer's disease progression. Safety profile was manageable with no dose-limiting toxicity preventing adequate exposure.
